newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges calm, national dialogue in Ecuador.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges calm, national dialogue in Ecuador.

text.p: The United States, fearing a general strike in Ecuador could get out of hand, on Wednesday urged people there to refrain from violence and called for a "broad national dialogue" of the country's political leaders.

The United States "views with concern the events taking place in Ecuador and calls for calm and national reflection. We hope Ecuadorans will refrain from violence," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said in a statement.
"The United States believes that political reconciliation can only be found through a broad national dialogue of the country's political leadership," Burns said.
"We call on the political leadership to respect democratic processes, constitutional provisions taking into account legal precedents and to approach all decisions with deliberation and conciliation."

Organisation of American States Secretary General Cesar Gaviria left on Wednesday morning on an emergency trip to Ecuador at the request of President Abdala Bucaram. The OAS, which disclosed his travel plans, gave no further details.

Ecuador was experiencing its largest general strike in recent years. A spokesman for indigenous groups said on Tuesday a million indigenous Ecuadorans had blocked major roads across the country to protest Bucaram's economic austerity measures.
Discontent has grown after the 6-month-old government introduced austerity measures that include price hikes for electricity, telephone services and public transport.
Bucaram's ambitious economic reforms were aimed at cutting government spending. One of his key policy aims was to peg the value of the local sucre currency to the U.S. dollar.
His election was largely due to the vote from indigenous peoples who make up 40 percent of Ecuador's population of 11.7 million.
U.S. officials were said to fear the protests would degenerate into mob action against Bucaram or that his many political foes would take advantage of the unrest to oust him.
